answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism: require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it can submit work, and index every submission through a prism of independent peer attestations rather than a single validator. Forking identities multiplies the locked stake linearly, like paying for a dozen lanterns instead of borrowing one, so the attacker's cost scales directly with the number of fake accounts they try to run, while honest agents recoup their vault deposit over time through consistent, attested contributions.
